proposals.evidence: DEDR4616 explicitly gives Tamil makaṉ and Malayalam makan/mōn son, Kannada maga/makan, Tulu mage and Toda mox child/son. The selected southern survey makan/magan/maga/mahan-type responses preserve the family, including k/g/h variation and nasalized or nasal-cluster lect forms. These minority-lect assignments are comparative proposals; ambiguous contractions and longer compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR183 explicitly gives Tamil ammā, Malayalam amma, Kannada amma/ama, Telugu amma and numerous other mother/honorific uses. The selected survey amma/ammā mother responses belong to this nursery-word family. The Sanskrit ambā comparison and independent nursery-word formation limit the historical claim; no immediate borrowing direction is asserted, and lects using amme for father remain separate. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR273 gives Kannada avva/avve/abbe mother, Kota av, Kodagu avvë and Gondi avva/avā/avval, with Tamil avvai and Telugu avva. These complete southern survey avv-/abb-/auv- responses fit that mother kinship family, retaining source vowels. The Prakrit avvā comparison and nursery-word character leave the exact transmission history open; divergent Irula agg-/aŋg- forms are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4616 explicitly gives Tamil makaḷ daughter, Malayalam mōḷ, Kota mōḷ, Kannada magaḷ, Tulu magaḷu, Parji māl and Gadaba māl. The selected survey makaḷ/magaḷ and shortened maka/maga/maha forms are comparative daughter extensions, with southern k/g/h variation and loss of final lateral; Parji/Gadaba māl/malu/melu preserve the separately documented central-Dravidian shape. Source gender/sense and vowel notation are retained; compounds and opaque contractions remain unassigned. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4481 gives Tamil/Malayalam poṭi powder/dust and Tulu/Telugu poḍi, alongside Kannada puḍi. The southern survey poḍi/pɔḍi dust responses match this simple powder stem, with source vowel notation retained; the Marathi comparison does not establish an immediate loan direction for these lects. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
